repairs.old_challenge: Jer.36.9-Jer.36.26: The final span differs from Jer.36.9-Jer.36.19 plus Jer.36.20-Jer.36.26.

new_challenge.claim: Verse 36:20 relocates the scroll from the officials' chamber to the king's winter house and begins a new royal audience: Jehudi reads, Jehoiakim cuts the columns, and the fire consumes them. Treating 36:9-26 as one scene obscures the completed temple-and-official inquiry at 36:19.
new_challenge.proposed_remedy: Segment Jer.36.9-Jer.36.19 as the temple reading and official inquiry and Jer.36.20-Jer.36.26 as the royal reading, burning, and arrest order; hydrate both beneath the existing Jer.36.9-Jer.36.26 scroll-escalation parent.

repairs.old_challenge: Jer.37.11-Jer.37.21: The final span differs from Jer.37.11-Jer.37.15 plus Jer.37.16-Jer.37.21.

new_challenge.claim: The notice that Jeremiah remained in the dungeon many days at 37:16 marks elapsed time and a scene change from gate arrest and beating to Zedekiah's secret consultation. The private word, counterquestion, custody petition, transfer, and bread allowance form a separate royal-interview resolution.
new_challenge.proposed_remedy: Expose Jer.37.11-Jer.37.15 and Jer.37.16-Jer.37.21 as two ordered children, with mandatory sibling hydration under Jer.37.11-Jer.37.21 so arrest causation remains connected to the later audience.

repairs.old_challenge: Jer.38.1-Jer.38.13: The final span differs from Jer.38.1-Jer.38.6 plus Jer.38.7-Jer.38.13.

new_challenge.claim: Ebedmelech hears what happened at 38:7 and becomes the new acting subject, leaving the gate court to petition the king before reversing the completed lowering into mud. His rescue commission, padded-rope procedure, and lifting action constitute a second scene rather than merely the tail of the officials' accusation.
new_challenge.proposed_remedy: Represent Jer.38.1-Jer.38.6 as accusation and cistern confinement and Jer.38.7-Jer.38.13 as Ebedmelech's intervention and rescue, returning both with a Jer.38.1-Jer.38.13 episode parent.

repairs.old_challenge: Jer.40.7-Jer.40.12: The final span differs from Jer.40.7-Jer.40.16.

new_challenge.claim: The field-command leadership introduced in 40:7 returns in 40:13 to address Gedaliah, while the warning tests the governorship and settlement policy just established. Cutting at 40:12 makes the harvest-gathering success appear resolved before the Ishmael threat exposes its fragility.
new_challenge.proposed_remedy: Retain Jer.40.7-Jer.40.12 and Jer.40.13-Jer.40.16 as distinct movements only if a mandatory Jer.40.7-Jer.40.16 administration-and-warning parent hydrates them together; otherwise merge that parent as the alternate unit.

repairs.old_challenge: Jer.40.13-Jer.40.16: The final span differs from Jer.40.7-Jer.40.16.

new_challenge.claim: Jer.40.13 changes from remnant-return narration to direct warning, yet Johanan's proposal and Gedaliah's refusal are consequences of the commander assembly and oath in 40:7-12. A bare 40:13-16 object loses the administrative setting and the identity continuity of those commanders.
new_challenge.proposed_remedy: Add one administration-and-warning parent spanning Jer.40.7-Jer.40.16. Its settlement child would cover verses 7-12, its warning child verses 13-16, and retrieval would be bidirectional; merging the parent is the fallback if hydration cannot be guaranteed.

repairs.old_challenge: Jer.41.11-Jer.41.18: The final span differs from Jer.41.11-Jer.41.15 plus Jer.41.16-Jer.41.18.

new_challenge.claim: Ishmael's escape with eight men closes the Gibeon pursuit at 41:15. Verse 41:16 then recapitulates the people Johanan recovered before moving to a Bethlehem-area encampment and an Egyptward strategy motivated by fear of Babylon, so rescue action has yielded to migration planning.
new_challenge.proposed_remedy: Surface Jer.41.11-Jer.41.15 as pursuit and captive recovery and Jer.41.16-Jer.41.18 as remnant regrouping and flight transition; hydrate the ordered siblings through their Jer.41.11-Jer.41.18 narrative parent.

repairs.old_challenge: Jer.42.7-Jer.42.22: The final span differs from Jer.42.7-Jer.42.18 plus Jer.42.19-Jer.42.22.

new_challenge.claim: The direct address to the remnant of Judah at 42:19 shifts from the reported stay-or-Egypt oracle to Jeremiah's prosecutorial application. Verses 20-22 look back on the commissioned prayer, accuse the hearers of self-deception, and restate the consequence, giving the passage a discrete indictment coda.
new_challenge.proposed_remedy: Use Jer.42.7-Jer.42.18 for the complete two-path divine answer and Jer.42.19-Jer.42.22 for the compliance indictment, while a Jer.42.7-Jer.42.22 parent preserves the answer-and-response sequence.

repairs.old_challenge: Jer.44.15-Jer.44.30: The final span differs from Jer.44.15-Jer.44.19 plus Jer.44.20-Jer.44.28 plus Jer.44.29-Jer.44.30.

new_challenge.claim: Three marked speech acts structure this disputation: the assembly answers Jeremiah at 44:15, Jeremiah turns to the men and women at 44:20, and the 'this shall be the sign' formula opens the Hophra oracle at 44:29. One surface hides the opponents' completed testimony, the prophetic rebuttal, and the corroborating royal sign as distinct forms.
new_challenge.proposed_remedy: Create hydrated children Jer.44.15-Jer.44.19 for the Queen-of-Heaven countertestimony, Jer.44.20-Jer.44.28 for the rebuttal and name-withdrawal oracle, and Jer.44.29-Jer.44.30 for the Pharaoh sign beneath Jer.44.15-Jer.44.30.

repairs.old_challenge: Jer.46.1-Jer.46.12: The final span differs from Jer.46.1-Jer.46.1 plus Jer.46.2-Jer.46.12.

new_challenge.claim: Jer.46.1 supplies the pan-national superscription, the word concerning the nations, whereas 46:2 opens the first nation-specific oracle with 'Of Egypt' and a dated Carchemish title. Combining them risks narrowing the collection heading to Egypt even when relation metadata separately records its wider scope.
new_challenge.proposed_remedy: Represent Jer.46.1 as a non-naked collection heading and Jer.46.2-Jer.46.12 as the dated Egypt battle oracle, with mandatory heading-scope hydration across the Jer.46.1-Jer.51.64 collection and no source-order preference.

repairs.old_challenge: Jer.48.11-Jer.48.17: The final span differs from Jer.48.11-Jer.48.20.

new_challenge.claim: The lament summons at 48:14-17 continues through Dibon and Aroer's commanded reactions in 48:18-20: descend, stand by the road, announce Moab's shame, and howl beside Arnon. The explicit judgment-on-the-plain formula at 48:21 offers a stronger catalogue onset than the town-address change at 48:18.
new_challenge.proposed_remedy: Extend the wine-metaphor and public-lament child through Jer.48.20, then begin a Jer.48.21-Jer.48.28 toponym catalogue and flight-call child; return both beneath the broader Jer.48.11-Jer.48.28 movement.

repairs.old_challenge: Jer.48.18-Jer.48.28: The final span differs from Jer.48.11-Jer.48.20 plus Jer.48.21-Jer.48.28.

new_challenge.claim: Beginning this unit at 48:18 bundles the closing public lament with a plateau-town judgment catalogue that announces itself only at 48:21. The Dibon-Aroer exchange answers the calamity and broken-staff cry from 48:16-17, while verses 21-24 switch to formal place-name enumeration.
new_challenge.proposed_remedy: Move Jer.48.18-Jer.48.20 into the preceding Jer.48.11-Jer.48.20 lament unit and narrow this child to Jer.48.21-Jer.48.28, retaining a mandatory Jer.48.11-Jer.48.28 parent for continuity.

repairs.old_challenge: Jer.51.1-Jer.51.14: The final span differs from Jer.51.1-Jer.51.10 plus Jer.51.11-Jer.51.19.

new_challenge.claim: Jer.51.11 resets the addressee with arrow-and-shield imperatives and names the kings of the Medes; temple vengeance, banner and ambush commands, and the oath at 51:14 then lead into the creator-idol hymn at 51:15-19. Ending at 51:14 bisects that mobilization-and-grounding movement and appends its first half to the destroying-wind testimony.
new_challenge.proposed_remedy: Repartition the material as Jer.51.1-Jer.51.10 and Jer.51.11-Jer.51.19, then hydrate those children with Jer.51.20-Jer.51.26 beneath a Jer.51.1-Jer.51.26 parent while preserving the received-order disclosure.

repairs.old_challenge: Jer.51.15-Jer.51.26: The final span differs from Jer.51.11-Jer.51.19 plus Jer.51.20-Jer.51.26.

new_challenge.claim: The anaphoric 'you are my war club' address at 51:20 opens a smashing litany after the creator-idol hymn closes with Jacob's portion at 51:19. Joining 51:15-26 suppresses that form and addressee reset, while starting at 51:15 also severs the hymn from the Medes-and-temple mobilization introduced at 51:11.
new_challenge.proposed_remedy: Close the middle child at Jer.51.19 after beginning it at Jer.51.11, and surface Jer.51.20-Jer.51.26 as the war-club and destroying-mountain oracle; hydrate both with the preceding Jer.51.1-Jer.51.10 child.

repairs.old_challenge: Jer.52.12-Jer.52.16: The final span differs from Jer.52.12-Jer.52.23.

new_challenge.claim: The fifth-month Nebuzaradan scene begins at 52:12 and continues through the Chaldeans' breaking and carrying of temple bronze in 52:17-23 without a new date, speaker, or principal agent. Verse 17 narrows the object from city and population to furnishings, but the repeated plunder actions can function as inventory elaboration within the same historical event.
new_challenge.proposed_remedy: Place Jer.52.12-Jer.52.16 and Jer.52.17-Jer.52.23 under a mandatory Jer.52.12-Jer.52.23 destruction-and-inventory parent, or merge that parent when the retrieval layer cannot guarantee both children.

repairs.old_challenge: Jer.52.17-Jer.52.23: The final span differs from Jer.52.12-Jer.52.23.

new_challenge.claim: Starting the bronze inventory at 52:17 recognizes a list-form shift, but the passage inherits its Chaldean agents and destructive sequence from 52:12-16. Naked retrieval would sever the pillars, sea, utensils, and measurements from the burning, wall demolition, deportation, and poor-remnant setting that explains their removal.
new_challenge.proposed_remedy: Keep the bronze inventory as a Jer.52.17-Jer.52.23 child only when retrieval also returns the 52:12-16 sibling and their 52:12-23 parent; exclude the renewed officer-and-execution action beginning at Jer.52.24.
